summary: Day was dominated by macro and politics, not company news. Democrats swept Congress; futures rose, gold went past $4,000, and BTC bounced about 5.5% on the day (position -4.2% on cost). Every held name's filings were checked: no 4.01, 4.02 or 5.02 items and no 1.01 deals on any holding. The only held name with earnings inside the 5-day window is CARG (11-05 after the close, file estimate 11-05). Held-name headlines were mild: Morgan Stanley raised IDXX to $810 (11-03) and Redburn to $700 (11-04) after the print, and Smart Insider flagged non-executive insider buying at MSM. DPZ has no filings or new headlines; the guidance-cut item flagged on 11-02 is still unconfirmed, with no 8-K and no echo in today's input. Non-held read-throughs: CVS beat and raised and announced a two-company split (H1 2028), SMG reported FY26 results with FY27 guidance in line, Apple guided December quarter revenue +7-10% with margin pressure from memory costs.

Regulators approving equity perpetual futures (11-03) is supportive, not adverse. Political risk (stricter oversight under a Democratic Congress) is a watch item and has not produced an action.
